title: Response to provincial changes to Guelph's Official Plan
subtitle: Heritage planning, view corridors, downtown park, letter to the Minister, and a heritage designation at 47 Alice Street.
overview: Council received a staff report on the Minister's decision to approve Official Plan Amendment 80 with modifications {{vote:m5}}. The decision is final and cannot be appealed. It allows much taller buildings downtown, shifts land in the Guelph Innovation District from employment toward housing and mixed use, and changes several specific sites. Staff have one year to update downtown zoning.

Council then set its response. Staff are to report back through the multi-year budget on financial and staffing impacts {{vote:m7}} and bring forward resources to speed up Cultural Heritage Action Plan work {{vote:m11}}. Staff will also consult the public on more view corridors in the next Official Plan review {{vote:m12}} and refer a downtown park plan to the 2024-2027 budget {{vote:m15}}. The Mayor will write to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing {{vote:m16}}. A clause on sending applications to the Grand River Conservation Authority was withdrawn.

Council also approved, on consent, notice of intention to designate 47 Alice Street under the Ontario Heritage Act and updates to the Building By-law. After a closed session, the Mayor reported that council received information on bargaining with two employee groups and gave staff direction.

decisions.detail: Council received the staff report on the Minister's decision to approve Official Plan Amendment 80 with modifications {{vote:m5}}.

decisions.item: Report on financial and staffing impacts
decisions.detail: Staff will report back through the multi-year budget on the financial and human resource impacts of OPA 80 and Bill 23 changes {{vote:m7}}.
Staff will bring forward through the multi-year budget the resources to speed up the action plan, including financial incentives for designated properties {{vote:m11}}.
In the next five-year Official Plan review, staff will consult the public and recommend added view corridors protecting sightlines to landmarks such as the Basilica {{vote:m12}}.
A plan for a future downtown park is referred to the 2024-2027 multi-year budget because of the higher heights and densities downtown {{vote:m15}}.
The Mayor is directed to write to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing about the impact of the OPA 80 amendments, based on the attached draft {{vote:m16}}.
The Clerk may publish notice of intention to designate 47 Alice Street, with a designation by-law to return if no objections are received in 30 days {{vote:m4}}.

debate: Councillors asked staff about effects of the changes. Staff said the downtown could now see up to 23 storeys, but each application is judged on its merits. Zoning updates may take up to a year, and applications can come in before then.

Some councillors raised concern about employment land. Staff said the reduction in the Guelph Innovation District changes the types of jobs expected, and that they cannot yet estimate effects because no development proposal has been submitted.

On the Conservation Authority clause, staff said new provincial rules limit the authority's comments on applications mostly to natural hazards, and that it asked the city not to send them. The mover withdrew the clause but wanted the concern on the public record.

Several councillors questioned whether the heritage, park and budget clauses were redundant, since staff said much of that work is already underway. Supporters said direction gives staff a mandate and reassures the community. Opponents worried about cost and about heritage work slowing development.

Debate on the letter was divided. Some said it would strain relations with the province and that the council's own decisions had contributed to the changes. Others said council has a duty to voice concerns, and that its plan met provincial housing targets.
